hook: A chip spy scandal, Anthropic IPO bets and Gemini 4 Carbon
summary: An Nvidia spy scandal puts Singapore chip intermediaries under scrutiny; Megaspeed reportedly bought $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips.
Nvidia plans to invest $10 billion in Anthropic around its IPO, while TSMC approved up to $500 million each for Anthropic and OpenAI.
Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to the public at $2 per million input tokens, and Fable 5.2 scored 41.3% on a freelance-work index.

stories.headline: Nvidia spy scandal exposes Singapore chip networks evading US export controls
stories.summary: The Nvidia spy scandal has exposed networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced U.S. AI chips and circumvent export controls. Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years.
stories.why_it_matters: The scandal brings heightened government scrutiny to the distribution networks and intermediary companies used to move advanced AI hardware across international borders.
source_titles: The Nvidia spy scandal exposes networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced US AI chips and circumvent export controls (Owen Walker/Financial Times)

stories.headline: TSMC to invest up to $1B in Anthropic and OpenAI at IPO price
stories.summary: TSMC has approved up to $500 million to buy shares in Anthropic at its IPO price and up to $500 million for preferred stock in OpenAI. The move follows Anthropic's IPO pricing of $70 to $78 per share and reflects TSMC's confidence in AI demand.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows a major chipmaker backing key AI developers, potentially influencing AI supply chains and investment flows.
source_titles: TSMC plans to invest up to $500M in Anthropic at its IPO price and up to $500M in OpenAI to acquire preferred stock (Reuters)

stories.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon to the public with agent swarm feature
stories.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Carbon to the general public via the Gemini API, the Gemini app and Antigravity, after a two-week limited release to cybersecurity defenders. The model is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens during an introductory period, and Google is previewing a "swarm" feature that turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents.
stories.why_it_matters: Google's public release of Carbon, priced well below rival frontier models, intensifies competition among the top AI labs and brings long-horizon agentic capabilities to a wider developer base.
source_titles: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature

stories.headline: Nvidia plans $10B investment in Anthropic alongside its IPO
stories.summary: Nvidia plans to invest $10 billion in Anthropic alongside its initial public offering. The commitment is part of a larger funding effort that includes public share sales and private deals with multiple technology giants.
stories.why_it_matters: The investment highlights the deepening financial ties between major artificial intelligence labs and hardware providers as they secure massive capital deployments.
source_titles: S-1: Nvidia plans to invest about $10B in Anthropic after its IPO, or ~10% of the new cash Anthropic is expected to raise this month, including in the IPO (Cory Weinberg/New York Times)

stories.headline: Fable 5.2 tops Remote Labor Index at 41.3% of freelance jobs
stories.summary: On the Remote Labor Index from Scale Labs and the Center for AI Safety, Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41.3% of real freelance projects at professional quality, ahead of Opus 5.5 (21.25%) and GPT 6 Astra (20.83%). The score is up from 2.5% for the top system a year ago.
stories.why_it_matters: The RLI measures how often AI output is acceptable to paying clients, making it a direct gauge of how close AI agents are to doing real freelance work.
source_titles: Scale Labs and CAIS' Remote Labor Index: Fable 5.2 completes 41.3% of freelance projects at professional quality, above Opus 5.5's 21.3% and GPT-6 Astra's 20.8% (Maximilian Schreiner/The Decoder)
